matches.quote: Give a table with thickness, geometry, growth method, contact configuration and contact resistance, excitation current and the extracted temperatures for every sample
The supporting diamagnetism (p. 5) is neither shown nor quantified for these samples... the diamagnetism discussion should be either backed by nanoflake magnetization data or softened.
The phase identity and structure of the measured flakes are not established, and the "relieved octahedral distortion" mechanism is not measured.
The statements that "the distortion in RuO6 octahedra is eliminated"... and that impurity-induced disorder "cannot explain this phenomenon"... are therefore assertions, not results
A phase entered at 220 K and left at about 100 K on cooling is a finite-temperature crossover, yet its boundaries are called "quantum critical points"
Samples 6 and 7 (50 nm on LaAlO3) have a shorter c axis (11.592 Å) and therefore... stronger RuO6 distortion, yet they show Bose-glass behaviour
Thickness does not order the phases, so the "thickness-tuned" framing is unsupported. Per the Fig. 1(a) legend, sample 4 (10 nm) and sample 5 (30 nm) are superconducting/Bose glass
The ρ ~ ln(1/T) versus σ ~ ln T discrimination rests on temperature windows too narrow to decide it... about 210-300 K for samples 1-3 (Fig. 2b)
The fixed choice p = 1 in L² = D T^(−p) (p. 7) ties length to temperature without justification.
In the Fisher framework the Bose glass is an insulating, compressible T = 0 phase with zero conductivity... "Mott insulator" in boson SIT language also differs
Field dependence of the drop, I-V characteristics, critical current and a Meissner signal are not shown; Ref. [20] is cited instead.
Per the Fig. 1(a) legend, sample 4 (10 nm) and sample 5 (30 nm) are superconducting/Bose glass, while samples 1 and 2 (25 nm) and sample 3 (35 nm) are Mott insulators

notes: C3 and C4 are general complaints about missing details referred to Ref. [20]; the review raises specific instances of missing characterization (superconductivity in P7, diamagnetism in P20, device/growth table in P15), counted as 'partly'. For C6, the review challenges whether octahedral distortion is relieved or controls correlations rather than disorder/composition (P12, P16) without asking for the microscopic theory of how distortion alters correlations, counted as 'partly'. For C9, P9 identifies the non-monotonic thickness ordering across 10, 25, 30, and 35 nm samples without specifically contrasting the Tc values of the 10 nm and 30 nm flakes, counted as 'partly'.
